summary.oneLiner: Niche, high-margin (≈55% standalone EBITDA) Indian molecular-diagnostics open-kit maker compounding ~15% domestic / ~20-25% export, now adding inorganic legs (TRUPCR Europe ~40% CAGR, Coris AMR in Belgium) funded by a ~INR230 cr cash/treasury war-chest earmarked for further M&A; key optionality = US FDA clearance for Coris AMR (Resist-5/Carba5) opening the largest global MDx market.

investment thesis (one-liner): Niche, high-margin (≈55% standalone EBITDA) Indian molecular-diagnostics open-kit maker compounding ~15% domestic / ~20-25% export, now adding inorganic legs (TRUPCR Europe ~40% CAGR, Coris AMR in Belgium) funded by a ~INR230 cr cash/treasury war-chest earmarked for further M&A; key optionality = US FDA clearance for Coris AMR (Resist-5/Carba5) opening the largest global MDx market.
guidance (critical — explicit): Revenue growth: 15-20% for FY27 (consolidated, all businesses) — reiterated multiple times, incl closing remarks.
EBITDA growth: also 15-20% ("same pace"); margin profile to "remain similar" — no major erosion expected on 3B.
Blended FY27 EBITDA margin (ex-other-income): ~40-45% (investor-built, mgmt said "hopefully"). 3B+TRUPCR EBITDA INR69.22 cr → grow ~15% → ~INR79 cr.
FY27 topline build (investor-confirmed by mgmt): 3B+TRUPCR ~INR107 cr → ~INR124-125 cr; Coris ~INR36 cr (7-mo) → ~INR52 cr (full yr); total ~INR175-180 cr.
Coris EBITDA: FY27 "slight EBITDA positive" (flat); 5-7% in FY28; ~10% by FY28-29. FY27 Q1 & Q2 will be LOSS-making (HAT order books in H2 / advance only).
Segment split of growth: domestic ~15% (only ~20% if seasonal flu/dengue spike), exports ~20-25%.
Cadence change: only TWO earnings calls/year going forward (half-yearly).
pipeline (new assays / regulatory approv: US FDA submission for Coris AMR — lead product Resist-5 / Carba5 (carbapenemase resistance panel), ~30-35% of Coris revenue; targeted FY28 opportunity. Lab tie-ups for clinical trials done; mgmt "confident" but timeline 1–1.5 yrs+ ("will definitely happen, only timing"). US rapid-AMR market ~INR100 cr / 10 m EUR. US could become ~20% of Coris revenue → 1-1.5 m EUR (INR11-16 cr), offsetting HAT runoff.

IVDR transition (EU) — BSI appointed as notified body; IVDR-aligned QMS audits completed; technical documentation review for key product families progressing. Seen as a competitive moat / barrier to Chinese imports.
Sample-to-answer system — via OEM (not in-house dev); validation ongoing, "initial results good"; expect 2-3 lab installs from Q3 FY27 onward (already baked into 15-20% guidance).
segment detail: 3B India (open-kit MDx): ~INR86.5 cr; dominant in oncology & higher multi-panels (respiratory, meningitis); ~15% share of INR500-600 cr Indian addressable market. Capacity utilisation only ~50%.
TRUPCR Europe (UK): INR20.67 cr, ~40% 4-yr CAGR; faces competition but managing.

Coris (Belgium, AMR rapid diagnostics): ~INR50 cr annualised; AMR is growth/margin driver; ~23% of remaining (non-AMR: respiratory, Entero) under Chinese low-price pressure; HAT contract = EUR6 m total (2024, 4-yr), ~EUR3.45 m executed, ~EUR2.4 m remaining through FY28 (Congo-specific, Ebola risk to timing).
growth / optionality: Oncology & genetic high-panel menu (pricing power; competition only from MNCs, no erosion).
Export expansion: Europe, Africa, Asia-Pacific, Middle East, Latin America; "lot of market where we are not present."
US FDA = largest lever (US = ~50% of global MDx; currently absent).
M&A roll-up funded by ~INR230 cr treasury (see §9).
Sample-to-answer (OEM) opens the ~30-35% of Indian market currently outside open-kit.
margins & cost: 3B standalone structurally ~55% EBITDA / ~60% GM — niche molecular = high margin.
Consolidated margin dragged to ~40% by Coris (~10% EBITDA) + TRUPCR (~15-20%).
Coris EBITDA depressed by high employee cost / large team; mgmt rationalising product costing toward 10% EBITDA over 1-2 yrs.
Q4 is the new cost baseline (full Coris + TRUPCR + 3B consolidation; employee & other expenses up 3-4x YoY on Coris).
capex: Minimal — running ~50% capacity; capacity addition would cost only ~INR4-5 cr. No large organic capex; growth is asset-light + inorganic.
capital allocation: ~INR230 cr cash/treasury; generating ~INR40 cr+ FCF/yr → recurring "cash pile" problem.
M&A budget ~INR140 cr flagged earlier; 3-4 consultants engaged (France, UK, US); "few advanced discussions," expect "something by year-end" (Q1/Q2 unlikely). Target by year-end FY27.

M&A criteria: topline ≥EUR2 m, growing sector, EBITDA-positive OR turnaround; broadening beyond hardcore IVD into adjacent diagnostics/molecular/genetics. Preferred multiples 6-8x vs sellers asking ~20x (valuation gap = key blocker).
Treasury mix: ~5-7% equity MF; ~30-35% FDs; ~30-35% treasury bonds; rest AAA corporate bonds (e.g., Tata Capital). Liquidatable within 3-4 days; FDs/bonds laddered to mature.
Plan to keep ~INR50 cr permanent reserve, deploy rest into M&A. Tax: Coris carry-forward EUR2-3 m → ~3-4 yrs no Coris tax.
risks: Domestic growth slowed to ~2-3% YoY last two quarters (post high FY24/25 base + FY25 flu/dengue exceptional INR4.2 cr).
Chinese low-cost competition in high-volume respiratory/Entero rapid tests (hits ~23% of Coris non-AMR mix).
Middle East geopolitical tension hit some export markets in FY26.
US FDA timeline uncertainty (could slip beyond 1.5 yrs).
HAT order is lumpy, Congo-specific, Ebola-exposed; one-time PAT contributor that fades.
Coris H1 FY27 EBITDA losses; consolidation of unprofitable quarters drags reported H1.
M&A execution risk — valuation gap (sellers at 20x).
management tone: Confident, candid, detailed on numbers. Repeatedly refused QoQ analysis ("quarter-on-quarter is very difficult"), pushing full-year framing — partly to deflect the soft domestic last-2-quarter trend. Transparent on one-offs (HAT, R&D amortisation, flu/dengue base). Disciplined on M&A valuation ("won't overpay at 20x"). Mildly impatient with investor's heavy arithmetic but cooperative.
non-obvious insights: The INR60 cr consolidated PAT is flattered by Coris's HAT order landing in the consolidated (profitable) 7-month window — sustainable Coris is barely EBITDA-positive.
"Only two earnings calls/year" going forward reduces disclosure cadence — watch for less granularity.
Renaming Kilpest → 3B BlackBio Dx completes identity shift to pure diagnostics.
Real moat = IVDR + (pending) US FDA as regulatory barriers that keep Chinese volume players out of AMR/oncology/high-panel niches.
Pricing chain: kit sold to distributor ~INR700-800 → hospital buys ~INR1,000 → end test billed ~INR2,000-2,500.
challenges → beneficiaries: Challenge: Chinese low-cost respiratory/rapid-test glut pressures commodity assays → beneficiary tilt: AMR/oncology/high-panel niche players (3B/Coris) with regulatory moats (IVDR/FDA). ✅ self-beneficiary via menu mix-shift to AMR.

Challenge: US AMR market import-dependent, FDA-gated → ⭐ optionality beneficiary = Coris Resist-5 on clearance (INR100 cr market, currently served by a French exporter via FDA-registered US distributor).
Beneficiaries (external listed names): none clearly identified.
qoq log: Q4 FY26 (this call): First call reflecting FULL consolidation of Coris (7 mo) + TRUPCR + 3B. Consol rev ~INR142 cr, PAT ~INR60 cr. Guidance FY27: 15-20% rev & EBITDA growth; topline build to ~INR175-180 cr. Coris EBITDA-flat FY27, 10% by FY28-29. US FDA (Resist-5) targeted FY28. IVDR QMS audits done (BSI). Sample-to-answer OEM installs from Q3 FY27. ~INR230 cr treasury, M&A "by year-end." Cadence cut to 2 calls/yr.
(Prior quarters referenced by mgmt: sample-to-answer & POC mentioned last call; M&A candidates met in Dubai; competition commentary unchanged QoQ. No structured prior note on file.)

themes.title: Medical devices & IVD
themes.need: Medical-device, consumable and IVD makers ride a manufacturing/export and Make-in-India import-substitution cycle - product/capex-driven, not hospital-footfall driven.
themes.driver: Export (US/EU/tariff) + Make-in-India import-substitution and product/capex cycle.
